symptoms: Young caterpillars eat the tender leaves of the plant.
Older caterpillars bore round holes into the fruit.
The caterpillar pushes part of its body inside the fruit to eat the inside.
You may see damaged fruits and caterpillars on the plants.
prevention: Plant American tall marigold and tomato seedlings together in a 1 to 16 row ratio.
Set up pheromone traps to catch the moths.
Use tomato nursery as a trap crop to attract egg-laying females.
practices: Regularly check your plants for damaged fruits and caterpillars.
Pick off and destroy any infected fruits and large caterpillars you find.
Install pheromone traps in the field and record the number of moths caught.
Remove and destroy trapped moths after each count.
